spots.bio: A surf beach on the south coast with a lookout view.
spots.name: Pennington Bay
spots.note: Kept: Wikivoyage says 'don't miss Pennington Bay' and the board features the view; a surf beach on the south coast. Placed inside Kangaroo Island, reached from the island's bases; no other destination exists nearby.

spots.bio: A climb of about 500 steps to a 360-degree view, which Matthew Flinders ascended in 1802.
spots.name: Prospect Hill
spots.note: Kept: Both sources: 500-step climb to a 360-degree view, Flinders ascended it in 1802. Placed inside Kangaroo Island, reached from the island's bases; no other destination exists nearby.

spots.bio: A 4 km white-sand swimming beach with a 100-year-old jetty and boat ramp, on the island's north coast.
spots.name: Emu Bay
spots.note: Kept: Tourism board names the 4 km white sand safe swimming beach with 100-year-old jetty and boat ramp; also covers the Emu Bay trilobite fossil shale (Emu Bay Shale merged here). Placed inside Kangaroo Island, reached from the island's bases; no other destination exists nearby.

spots.bio: The island's largest town, with a harbour and the site of South Australia's first European settlement.

spots.name: Kingscote
spots.note: Kept: Wikivoyage and tourism board give Kingscote its own section: island's largest town, harbour and first European settlement of South Australia. Placed inside Kangaroo Island, reached from the island's bases; no other destination exists nearby.

spots.bio: The site of South Australia's first settlement, with a lookout, the Mulberry Tree and interpretive signs.
spots.name: Reeves Point
spots.note: Kept: Both sources: site of South Australia's first settlement, lookout, famous Mulberry Tree, interpretive signs. Placed inside Kangaroo Island, reached from the island's bases; no other destination exists nearby.

spots.bio: A free daily pelican feeding behind the Marine Centre in Kingscote.
spots.name: Kingscote Pelican Feeding
spots.note: Kept: Wikivoyage names the free daily 5pm pelican feeding behind the Marine Centre as a Kingscote wildlife stop; permanent daily activity, about half an hour. spots.bio: A 25 m silo mural of a kangaroo and a glossy black cockatoo at Kingscote.
spots.name: Kingscote Silo Art
spots.note: Kept: Board features the 25 m kangaroo and glossy black cockatoo silo mural ('you can't miss'); a roadside icon. Placed inside Kangaroo Island, reached from the island's bases; no other destination exists nearby.

spots.bio: A jetty used for fishing and sunsets, with leafy sea dragons around the pylons for snorkellers.
spots.name: Kingscote Jetty
spots.note: Kept: Board names the jetty for fishing, sunset and snorkelling for leafy sea dragons around the pylons; a jetty a guide names. Placed inside Kangaroo Island, reached from the island's bases; no other destination exists nearby.

spots.bio: An 1856 cottage holding a collection of Kangaroo Island heritage.
spots.name: Hope Cottage National Trust Museum
spots.note: Kept: Board names the museum's 'outstanding collection' of island heritage in an 1856 cottage; small museum visitors can enter. Placed inside Kangaroo Island, reached from the island's bases; no other destination exists nearby.

spots.bio: A fishing village on Pelican Lagoon with a wharf, the Independence replica, walks, wildlife and oysters.

spots.name: American River
spots.note: Kept: Both sources give the fishing village its own section: wharf, Independence replica and rebuild shed, walks, wildlife, oysters. Placed inside Kangaroo Island, reached from the island's bases; no other destination exists nearby.

spots.bio: Red-orange cliffs about 15 minutes north of American River, best at sunset.
spots.name: Red Banks Beach
spots.note: Kept: Tourism board names the colourful red-orange cliffs 15 min north of American River, best at sunset; a second-tier scenic stop. Minimal facilities. Placed inside Kangaroo Island, reached from the island's bases; no other destination exists nearby.
